title: Plan regression (automatic plan correction)
summary: A front-desk visit summary whose plan depends on the first range it's compiled for: a few patients seek (plan A); then the runner recompiles it for every patient, so the cached plan scans care.appointments (plan B), and the same narrow lookups go on far more slowly. With FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN on, Azure SQL Database's default, automatic tuning forces plan A. In the Database Agent beat (2026-11-18) the run holds it off until Database Agents raises its issue, then forces the last good plan itself and puts it back. T3 (Azure SQL Database) only.

concurrency.description: Sessions running the lookups; session 1 also unforces an earlier run's forced plan at the start and makes the switch, and in the Database Agent beat holds automatic correction and makes the response. Up to 8 so the beat's regressed lookups can load T3's two vCores (2026-11-18).

intensity.description: Pace: a lookup about every 400 ms per session at 1, back to back at 10.

notes.T3: The runner signs in to T3 as the P6 group's member, a database owner, so it can recompile the lookup (sp_recompile), unforce an earlier run's forced plan (sp_query_store_unforce_plan), and, in the Database Agent beat, turn FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN off and back on (ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET AUTOMATIC_TUNING) and force the last good plan (sp_query_store_force_plan); it touches only demo.usp_visit_summary_lookup's plans and that one database option. SQL Server 2022 Standard on T1 and T2 has no automatic tuning, and the procedure refuses to run there.

goodPercent.description: The share of the run on plan A, before the switch to plan B.

respondPercent.description: The Database Agent beat (2026-11-18): at this share of the run, session 1 makes the manual response Database Agents' guidance asks for, forcing the last good plan through Query Store (the plan sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations recommends, or the lookup's plan with the lowest average CPU). 0 makes none; otherwise above goodPercent.

holdAutoCorrection.description: The Database Agent beat (2026-11-18): session 1 turns FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN off for the run, so the regression lasts until Database Agents raises its issue, and puts it back as it found it at the response, at the run's end, or, when the run ends any other way, at auto-cleanup, the next run's start, reset, or setup.

pauseMs.description: The pause between one session's lookups in milliseconds; 0 takes it from the intensity. The Database Agent beat sets a short one, so the scans of the regressed plan load T3's CPU while the seeks of the good plan barely do (2026-11-18).

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerCPUUtilization: a step up at the switch, and down again once automatic tuning forces plan A
sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations: a FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN recommendation for demo.usp_visit_summary_lookup's query, Verifying or Success once it's applied
expectedHubSignals.note: Also on the Azure portal's automatic tuning page for the database. The DMV shows the regression whether or not FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN is on; with it on, the plan is forced when the estimated CPU gain is over 10 seconds.

expectedHubSignals.signal: A plan regression or forced-plan finding for the lookup
expectedHubSignals.note: Preview; coverage by target is undocumented (ADR 0013).

expectedHubSignals.signal: In the Database Agent beat (holdAutoCorrection, respondPercent): an issue on T3 for the regressed lookup (long-running query, high CPU, or query plan regression; Learn doesn't say which a plan regression raises), with Analyze slow query under its captured query for long-running query and high CPU issues; after the response it closes at the agent's next check
expectedHubSignals.note: Database Agents (preview) supports Azure SQL Database in Database Hub: about 15 minutes to a new issue, contextual AI for high CPU and long-running query issues only, and no change applied by the agent; T3 must be selected once under Manage agents (Learn: database-agents).

expectedSymptoms: Before the switch, each lookup reads a few dozen pages; after it, each lookup scans care.appointments
Query Store shows one query with two plans, and the later one regressed on CPU and duration
Within minutes of enough regressed executions, automatic tuning forces plan A and the lookups are fast again
queryLevelEvidence: Query Store's Regressed Queries and Queries With Forced Plans reports (SSMS), and sys.query_store_plan.is_forced_plan
sys.dm_db_tuning_recommendations: the reason, the estimated CPU gain, and the state, with the plan IDs in its details
reset: The lookups only read. A forced plan stays after the run, so it can be shown; the next plan-regression run, or reset, unforces it (sp_query_store_unforce_plan, for demo.usp_visit_summary_lookup's queries only). A hold on FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN goes back as the run found it at the response or the run's end, and otherwise at auto-cleanup, the next run's start, reset (auto-tuning-restored), or setup.
